q: When a charge is given to a conducting object of any shape, the charge is found to be spread out over the ____ of the object.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. When a charge is given to a conducting object of any shape, the charge is found to be spread out over the outer surface of the object.

q: But the charge is not ____ distributed.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. But the charge is not uniformly distributed.

q: The more highly curved parts of the objects have ____ of charge than the less curved parts.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The more highly curved parts of the objects have greater concentration of charge than the less curved parts.

q: Therefore, we can say that charges are highly concentrated at the ____ of the object.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Therefore, we can say that charges are highly concentrated at the pointed portion of the object.

q: For a charged pointed rod shown in Figure 9.5(d) the charge concentration at the pointed end is so large that some of the charges ____ into the air.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. For a charged pointed rod shown in Figure 9.5(d) the charge concentration at the pointed end is so large that some of the charges leak off into the air.

q: This makes a pointed rod very useful as a ____.
e: This makes a pointed rod very useful as a lightning conductor. Lightning conductor is what this statement is using.

q: However, the electric fields due to the individual charges on the surface of the charged conducting object all ____ inside the object.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. However, the electric fields due to the individual charges on the surface of the charged conducting object all cancel out inside the object.

q: Therefore, the electric field is ____ everywhere inside a charged conducting object of any shape.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. Therefore, the electric field is zero everywhere inside a charged conducting object of any shape.

q: The motion of charges or the current is not observed in a charged conducting object, because there is ____ inside it.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The motion of charges or the current is not observed in a charged conducting object, because there is no electric field inside it.

q: If the electric field intensity varies from point to point in an electric field, such an electric field is called a ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. If the electric field intensity varies from point to point in an electric field, such an electric field is called a non-uniform electric field.

q: For example, the electric field around a ____ is a non-uniform electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. For example, the electric field around a point charge is a non-uniform electric field.

q: The electric lines of force which represent a non-uniform electric field are not parallel but are ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric lines of force which represent a non-uniform electric field are not parallel but are continuous curves.

q: If the electric field intensity at every point is the same in magnitude and direction, such an electric field is called a ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. If the electric field intensity at every point is the same in magnitude and direction, such an electric field is called a uniform electric field.

q: For example, the electric field between two ____ is a uniform electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. For example, the electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is a uniform electric field.

q: As shown in Figure 9.6 a uniform electric field is represented by electric lines of force which are ____ of the same length.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. 6 a uniform electric field is represented by electric lines of force which are uniformly spaced parallel lines of the same length.
